The Best Highlighter Pens
August 4, 2026 - Posted by Connie to Guides, Pens, Markers and Felt Tip Pens, Highlighters

Highlighters are useful pens for anyone wanting to draw attention to important information in notes. Keep reading to find out how to choose a highlighter and recommendations for specific uses.

TOP CHOICE: ZEBRA JUSTFIT MOJINI LINE HIGHLIGHTERS
The Zebra Justfit Mojini Line because of its impressive compatibility with all kinds of writing instruments.

Shop Now

Our top choice is the Zebra Justfit Mojini Line because of its impressive compatibility with all kinds of writing instruments. Its ink is specially designed to resist smudging inks, including those from rollerball pens and inkjet printing. The Justfit Mojini Line has a flexible chisel tip that follows the curves of thick books, creating consistent lines. Choose from five colors, all of which stand out without being fluorescent.

HIGHLIGHTER PEN CONSIDERATIONS
Highlighter Types
There are three main highlighter types: ink, gel, and pencil.
There are three main highlighter types. Most highlighters use liquid inks and work like felt tip pens or markers. They come in the widest selection of colors, tip features, and body designs. However, highlighters with broad tips or wet ink flow may bleed through the paper and leave marks on the back side of the page. Pick an ink highlighter if you want to color-code your notes.

Like its name suggests, a gel highlighter marks paper with a gel stick rather than ink. It’s designed to be more resistant to bleedthrough and smudging, but it’s also less precise. It may leave gel “crumbs” behind on the paper, which can smear when brushed over with your hand. Gel highlighters are great for low-quality paper and inkjet printouts.

Pencil highlighters are like bright colored pencils or lead holders. They won’t bleed through paper at all and don’t need any time to dry. However, they may take several strokes to highlight a full line of text and are often better suited to underlining. Woodcased pencil highlighters need to be sharpened, which can be inconvenient. Clutch-style pencil highlighters are refilled by replacing the entire lead. We recommend pencil highlighters when you’re working with low-quality paper that ink highlighters bleed through, or glossy paper that liquid highlighters take a lot of time to dry on.

Text Smearing
Some highlighters react to ink and cause it to smear, even if the text is completely dry.
Some highlighters react to ink and cause it to smear, even if the text is completely dry. As a general rule, gel pen ink, fountain pen ink, and inkjet printing are the most likely to react with highlighters. Gel highlighters are often a better choice for fountain pen inks, but they can cause ballpoint ink to feather. Smearing depends on the formula of the highlighter and writing ink as well as the paper, so it’s always best to test your combination before you start highlighting.

If you’re using fountain pens, check out our fountain pen ink comparisons for resistance tests against gel and liquid highlighters.

Bleedthrough & Showthrough
Because they put down a lot of ink, highlighters can bleed through low-quality papers and even leave marks on the other side.
Because they put down a lot of ink, highlighters can soak through low-quality papers and even leave marks on the other side. This is called bleedthrough. Inks are more likely to bleed on thin or highly absorbent paper (like printer paper). You can reduce showthrough and bleeding by choosing highlighters that deposit less ink or are specifically formulated to not bleed. Additionally, try using higher quality paper where possible.
Tip Shapes
While most highlighters have chisel tips, some feature small chisel tips, bullet tips, or brush tips.
When you think of a highlighter, you probably imagine a chisel-shaped tip. However, many highlighters are double sided with bullet tips on the opposite end, so you can also use them to underline or write out headers. Some highlighters have more unique tip options that offer convenience or are simply fun to use.
Brightness
Though all highlighters help make text stand out, their brightness can vary.
Though all highlighters help make text stand out, the brightness of their inks can vary. Fluorescent highlighters are the brightest and grab your attention. We should note that neon inks are hard to capture on camera and are much brighter in person.

Pastel highlighters are great for those who prefer softer colors. We noticed that yellow pastel highlighters tend to skew golden or orange.

Of course, there are options that aren’t neon or pastel. They catch your eye with bright hues that don’t rely on fluorescence.

Colors
Zebra Mildliner Highlighters come in a variety of vibrant and pastel colors.
Highlighters traditionally come in fluorescent yellow, but many come in a variety of colors to allow for color-coding. We recommend keeping your color palette to a few contrasting hues rather than a gradient of a dozen colors. Fewer colors means that it’s easier to remember your color key if you have one, and it prevents your notes from becoming so colorful that it’s hard to remember what’s going on.

Additionally, if you find fluorescent hues to be more distracting than helpful, there are pastel highlighters available to gently guide your attention.

HIGHLIGHTER PEN RECOMMENDATIONS
The Best Highlighter Pens for Color-Coding: Zebra Mildliner Double-Sided Highlighters
Zebra Mildliner Double-Sided Highlighters are excellent for color-coding, so it’s no wonder that they’re our most popular highlighters.

Shop Now

Zebra Mildliner Double-Sided Highlighters are excellent for color-coding, so it’s no wonder that they’re our most popular highlighters. They come in many more colors than other highlighters do, including some that are more vibrant than the “mild” in their name implies. These bolder shades are better for underlining or circling.

Mildliners have both chisel and fine tips to let you highlight large areas or underline specific words. However, because they tend to smear inks, you should be careful about what inks you pair them with.

If you love the Mildliner, check out the brush and marker versions, too.

Also Consider: KOKUYO Mark+ Highlighters

Try the KOKUYO Mark+ Highlighter if you’d rather not switch pens when changing colors. It features two chisel tips next to each other on the same end, so you can use a different color just by turning the pen in your hand.

Choose from two versions: the Dual Color pairs colored and gray inks, while the Dual Tone pairs a colored ink with a softer hue of the same color.

The Best Highlighter Pens for Written Notes: Staedtler Textsurfer Classic Highlighters
The Staedtler Textsurfer Classic is our go-to for written notes.

Shop Now

The Staedtler Textsurfer Classic is our go-to for written notes. It didn’t affect ballpoint, gel, rollerball inks in our tests, nor did it smear inkjet printing. It did smudge fountain pen ink, but not so much that it was unusable. Its lightfast, pigment-based ink showed through paper but didn’t bleed through. Keep in mind that your particular combination of ink and paper could smudge, so be sure to test it first.

The broad chisel tip is best for highlighting 12 point text and writing on standard rulings like 6 mm rule, but its point can make thinner lines.

The Best Highlighter Pens for Bibles and Thin Paper: Kutsuwa HiLiNE Highlighter Pencils
The Kutsuwa HiLiNE uses a soft core like that of a colored pencil which will never bleed.

Shop Now

The best way to keep ink from bleeding through the thin paper used for bibles is to not use ink at all! The Kutsuwa HiLiNE uses a soft core like that of a colored pencil which will never bleed. It puts down a fluorescent line that isn’t as bright as an ink highlighter, so it attracts your attention without being too strong.

The HiLiNE comes with a sharpener cap. When sharpening the pencil, twist the pencil gently until it comes to a blunt point. Sharpening too much may cause the lead to break easily.

The Best Highlighter Pens for Books: Staedtler Triplus Textsurfers
The Staedtler Triplus Textsurfer works well for highlighting book passages.

Shop Now

The Staedtler Triplus Textsurfer works well for highlighting book passages. Its flexible bullet tip is surprisingly versatile since you can use the tip’s side to highlight passages, or the point for underlining. In our tests, we noticed slight bleeding on printer paper, but no bleed or showthrough in books. However, since paper quality can vary, be sure to test your highlighter on a blank page first.

Like other Triplus Pens, the Textsurfer has a slim, triangular body. You can throw a handful into your pen case without taking up too much space.

Also Consider: Tombow Kei Coat & MONO Edge Highlighters

The Tombow Kei Coat and MONO Edge have chisel tips that are reinforced on two sides with plastic to prevent fraying. They also have fine tips on the other ends. As with the Textsurfer, there was no bleedthrough in books in our tests.

The Best Highlighter Pens for Textbooks: Kutsuwa Neonpitsu Knock Highlighter Pencils
The Kutsuwa Neonpitsu Knock is a pencil highlighter that takes no time to dry.

Shop Now

Most textbooks use thick paper with a glossy finish, so highlighter ink takes extra time to dry. To combat this, it’s a good idea to use a pencil highlighter like the Kutsuwa Neonpitsu Knock. It comes with a brightly colored 3.8 mm lead. Hold it perpendicular to the paper for a broad stroke, and use the edge for a thinner line. You can replace the lead when it runs out as well.
The Best Highlighter Pens for Inkjet Printouts: Uni Propus Window Soft Color Double-Sided Highlighters
The Uni Propus Window Soft Color Double-Sided Highlighter doesn’t smear inkjet printing.

Shop Now

Inkjet printouts tend to smear under highlighters, but not when paired with the Uni Propus Window Soft Color Double-Sided Highlighter. We appreciate that it comes with a handy window in the chisel tip so you can see where you’re highlighting. The opposite end has a bullet tip for more precise marks.

The highlighter’s pastel hues are also easier on the eyes. If you prefer brighter colors, the standard Uni Propus Window smeared inkjet printouts slightly.

Also Consider: Staedtler Textsurfer Gel Highlighters

The Staedtler Textsurfer Gel Highlighter puts down a smooth, fluorescent line that doesn’t smear inkjet printing or bleed through printer paper. Its broad, crayon-like tip wears down as you use it, so it’s best for highlighting large areas.

The Best Highlighter Pens for Photocopying and Triplicate Paper: Monami Essenti Soft Highlighters
The Monami Essenti Soft Highlighter won’t show up when copied, and it doesn’t fade over time when used on triplicate paper.

Shop Now

If you make a lot of copies, whether photocopies or triplicate paper, the Monami Essenti Soft Highlighter is a great option. Its ink won’t show up when copied, and it doesn’t fade over time when used on triplicate paper. We appreciate its spring-loaded clip, which lets you attach the highlighter over a stack of papers.
The Best Dual-Tip Highlighter Pens: KOKUYO Mark+ 2 Way Marker Pens
KOKUYO Mark+ 2 Way Marker Pens come in two versions to help you highlight with coordinating colors.

Shop Now

KOKUYO Mark+ 2 Way Marker Pens come in two versions to help you highlight with coordinating colors. The Gray Type includes a fineliner that’s a gray-tinted version of the chisel color, while the Color Type has a fineliner that’s a darker version of the chisel color. The Mark+ 2 Way allows you to highlight and write notes without switching to another pen.

On absorbent papers like cheap paperback pages, we noticed that the fineliner bled through slightly. Writing with the fineliner over any highlighting feathered badly, too.

Also Consider: Sun-Star Ninipie Dual Tip Highlighters

The innovative design of the Sun-Star Ninipie packs a chisel tip and fineliner marker on the same side. You can switch between highlighting and writing with a quick turn of the pen. The chisel tip’s highlighter color comes in your choice of vivid or pastel hues, while the fineliner can be complementary or contrasting.

Like the Mark+ 2 Way Marker Pen, we found the fineliner bled through slightly on rough paper at the end of the line. There’s also a slight learning curve to the Ninipie. Be sure to hold it steady to prevent accidentally switching between tips.

The Best Erasable Highlighter Pens: Pilot FriXion Light Erasable Highlighters
The Pilot FriXion Light uses thermosensitive ink that turns clear when exposed to heat, so you can “erase” any accidental over-highlighting.

Shop Now

The Pilot FriXion series uses one of our favorite ink formulations, so we have to recommend the highlighter version here. Its thermosensitive ink turns clear when exposed to heat, so you can “erase” any accidental over-highlighting. Simply rub over the ink with the built-in hard rubber “eraser.”

However, we should warn that the “erasing” works best on printed text. Using the “eraser” on some writing inks will cause it to smear or lighten. Be sure to test your pen and highlighter combination first.

Also Consider: Writech Erasable Highlighters

Instead of a thermosensitive ink, the Writech Erasable Highlighter uses an ink eraser to make highlighter ink disappear. However, keep in mind that you can’t go back over a spot where the ink eraser was applied.

The Best Fast-Drying Highlighter Pens: Pilot Kire-Na Double-Sided Highlighters
The Pilot Kire-Na was specifically formulated to dry quickly.

Shop Now

Winner of the 2025 Japan Stationery Awards Grand Prize, the Pilot Kire-Na was specifically formulated to dry quickly. In fact, it dries in just two seconds on the high-quality Rhodia paper we used in our tests.

Its most exciting feature is the guard rail around its chisel tip, which helps you draw straight lines and prevents ink from pooling at the end of a line. We love that its chisel tip is also flexible, so it follows curved textbook pages.

The Best Fun Highlighter Pens: Zebra Kirarich Highlighters
Zebra Kirarich Highlighters put down inks that are infused with silver and pulverized glass.

Shop Now

Dazzling Zebra Kirarich Highlighters put down inks that are infused with silver and pulverized glass. Kirakira (キラキラ) is a mimetic word for something sparkling, and the Kirarich’s twinkling lines make your notes a little more fun to read through. Try using them to add shimmer to your art, too!

We should warn that the Kirarich is a very wet highlighter. It’ll bleed through low-quality papers, and it takes a lot of time to dry.

Also Consider: Epoch Kobaru Sweet Tapir Scented Highlighters

The Epoch Kobaru Highlighter is filled with deliciously scented ink. It’s easiest to smell when the highlighter is uncapped and lingers for several minutes on the page. It has a thin, double-sided body design and soft pastel colors.

The Best Highlighter Pens for Left-Handers: Uni Propus Window Q-Dry Highlighters
The Uni Propus Window Q-Dry Highlighter dries quickly so left-handed writers don’t have to worry about accidental smudges.

Shop Now

The Uni Propus Window Q-Dry Highlighter dries incredibly quickly, so left-handed writers don’t have to worry about accidental smudges. Its built-in window ensures that you can see exactly where you’re highlighting, too. The other side of the pen has a bullet tip for circling and underlining.
The Best Precise Highlighter Pens: Monami Essenti Twin Highlighters
We like the Monami Essenti Twin Highlighter for precise highlighting thanks to its 2 mm chisel tip.

Shop Now

We like the Monami Essenti Twin Highlighter for precise highlighting thanks to its 2 mm chisel tip. We especially recommend pairing it with planners, which typically have more compact sheet styles than standard notebooks. It also has a 4 mm chisel tip on the other end for highlighting larger text.
Also Consider: Zebra Click Bright Highlighters

A retractable highlighter like the Zebra Click Bright is wonderfully convenient. You can quickly deploy the tip when it’s time to highlight, and you don’t have to worry about losing a cap.

The Best Refillable Highlighter Pens: Zebra Optex 1 EZ Highlighters
The Zebra Optex 1 EZ uses refillable cartridges that save you money and reduce waste.

Shop Now

Those who use highlighters a lot will appreciate the Zebra Optex 1 EZ. It uses refillable cartridges that save you money and reduce waste. The EZ in its name refers to how easy it is to pop off the cap. Just squeeze the two tabs, and it comes right off.
HIGHLIGHTER PEN TEST RESULTS

We performed our tests with yellow (or the closest possible color) highlighters for consistency. Please keep in mind that other colors in the same line may perform differently. When product lines included both neon and pastel colors, we tested both versions to check for differences in ink formulation and color intensity.

Dry Time & Showthrough

We tested dry times and showthrough on both 80 gsm Rhodia DotPad paper and standard copy paper. For double-sided highlighters, we used the broadest, chisel-shaped side for our tests. If the highlighter bled through the paper, we recorded it as having high or very high showthrough.

Click here to show dry time and showthrough test results.
Text Smearing

We tested each highlighter with the following products:

Ballpoint Pen: 0.5 mm Uni Jetstream Ballpoint Pen
Gel Pen: 0.5 mm Uni-ball Signo Gel Pen
Rollerball Pen: 0.7 mm Uni-ball Air Rollerball Pen
Pencil: Blackwing 602 Pencil (Firm Lead)
Fountain Pen: Fine TWSBI ECO Fountain Pen with Herbin Perle Noire

We created our samples on 80 gsm Rhodia DotPad paper, then let inks dry for at least fifteen minutes before going over them with each highlighter. Different pens and inks use different ink formulas, and the paper you write on can make ink more or less likely to smear. Be sure to test your combination of ink and paper.

Click here to show text smearing test results.
Brightness

We tested brightness on 80 gsm Rhodia DotPad paper. Click through to each product for writing samples. Be aware that photographing fluorescence is extremely difficult and fluorescent highlighters look brighter in person than in images.

Whether you’re studying for a test, editing an article, or taking notes, a highlighter is the ideal tool to help you remember information and draw attention to important points.
